steps: Set an adjustable bench to 30-45 degrees incline.
Sit with dumbbells on your thighs, then lie back and press them to shoulder width.
Lower the dumbbells with control until your elbows are at about 90 degrees.
Press back up, squeezing your upper chest at the top.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted and feet planted throughout.
mistakes: Setting the bench too steep (over 45°) shifts work to front delts.
Flaring elbows out to 90° strains the shoulder joint.
Bouncing the dumbbells off the chest reduces muscle tension.
incline_db_press.tip: Start lighter than your flat bench press; the incline reduces mechanical advantage.

steps: Lie on a flat bench with eyes under the barbell.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, wrists straight.
Unrack, lower to mid-chest with elbows at ~45-75° from torso.
Press up in a slight arc back over your shoulders.
Keep shoulder blades pinched and feet driving into the floor.
mistakes: Elbows flared to 90° increases shoulder impingement risk.
Bouncing the bar off the chest reduces pec engagement.
Losing upper-back tightness destabilizes the press.
flat_bb_bench.tip: Drive with your legs to create full-body tension and protect your shoulders.

steps: Set cable at lowest position, stand sideways to the stack.
Grip handle with outside hand, arm across body.
Raise arm out to side until elbow reaches shoulder height.
Pause briefly, then lower with control.
Keep a slight bend in the elbow throughout.
mistakes: Leaning away from the cable reduces side delt tension.
Raising above shoulder height shifts work to traps.
Using momentum instead of controlled movement.
cable_lateral_raise.tip: Cables provide constant tension — don't let the weight stack touch down between reps.

steps: Sit or stand, hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Keep elbows pointed forward, upper arms by ears.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending elbows.
Stretch until you feel a deep stretch in the triceps.
Extend arms back up, squeezing the triceps at the top.
mistakes: Flaring elbows out reduces long-head stretch.
Arching the lower back compensates for limited shoulder mobility.
Using too much weight limits range of motion.
overhead_triceps_ext.tip: If shoulder mobility is limited, do this one arm at a time with a lighter dumbbell.

steps: Start in plank position, hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Lower body until chest nearly touches the floor.
Keep elbows at ~45° from torso, core tight.
Push back up to full arm extension.
Maintain a straight line from head to heels throughout.
mistakes: Sagging hips or piking up breaks core tension.
Flaring elbows wide stresses the shoulders.
Incomplete range of motion (not going low enough).
pushups.tip: Elevate hands on a bench if full push-ups are too hard; progress to the floor over time.

steps: Sit at the machine, thighs under pads, grip bar wide.
Lean back slightly (~15°), chest up, shoulder blades down.
Pull the bar to upper chest, driving elbows down and back.
Squeeze lats at the bottom, pause briefly.
Return with control, allowing full stretch at the top.
mistakes: Pulling behind the neck strains the shoulder joint.
Leaning back excessively turns it into a row.
Using momentum / swinging the torso.
lat_pulldown.tip: Think 'pull elbows to pockets' rather than 'pull bar down' to engage lats better.

steps: Set chest pad height so your chest rests comfortably.
Grip handles, arms extended, shoulder blades protracted.
Row by driving elbows back, retracting shoulder blades.
Pull until hands are near hips, squeeze mid-back.
Lower with control, allowing full protraction at the bottom.
mistakes: Pulling with arms only, not retracting shoulder blades.
Chest coming off the pad reduces stability.
Shrugging traps up instead of depressing them.
chest_supported_row.tip: The chest support removes lower-back fatigue — focus purely on mid-back contraction.

steps: Set bench to 45-60° incline, sit back with dumbbells.
Let arms hang straight down, palms facing forward.
Curl dumbbells up, keeping elbows stationary behind torso.
Squeeze biceps at top, lower with control.
Get a full stretch at the bottom each rep.
mistakes: Bringing elbows forward loses the stretch on the long head.
Swinging the weights uses momentum, not biceps.
Not lowering fully misses the stretched-position benefit.
incline_db_curl.tip: The incline stretches the long head — that's where the growth happens. Don't cheat the stretch.

steps: Set cable at face height, rope attachment.
Step back, arms extended, slight stagger stance.
Pull rope toward face, separating hands, elbows high.
Rotate hands back so thumbs point behind you.
Squeeze rear delts and hold briefly, return slowly.
mistakes: Pulling to neck/chin instead of face level.
Dropping elbows low turns it into a row.
Using too much weight, losing external rotation.
face_pull.tip: Light weight, high reps (15-20), perfect form — this is for shoulder health, not ego.

steps: Stand tall, barbell at thighs, grip shoulder-width.
Keep elbows pinned to sides, curl bar to shoulders.
Squeeze biceps hard at the top.
Lower with control, don't let gravity drop it.
Keep wrists neutral, not bent back.
mistakes: Swinging torso/hips to move the weight.
Elbows drifting forward reduces biceps tension.
Curling only halfway down misses the stretch.
barbell_curl.tip: Strict form > heavy weight. Your biceps are small — they don't need momentum.

steps: Set bar on upper traps (high-bar) or rear delts (low-bar).
Feet shoulder-width, toes out 15-30°, brace core.
Descend by sitting back and down, knees tracking toes.
Go to at least parallel (hip crease below knee).
Drive up through mid-foot, chest up, knees out.
mistakes: Knees caving in (valgus) stresses the knee joint.
Heels rising shifts load to knees and reduces glute drive.
Rounding the lower back under load risks injury.
squat.tip: Learn to brace: big breath into belly, push abs out like you're taking a punch.

steps: Hold bar at hip width, feet hip-width, slight knee bend.
Hinge at hips, push butt back, bar slides down thighs.
Keep back flat, chest up, go until you feel hamstring stretch.
Stop when torso is ~parallel or stretch is maximal.
Drive hips forward to stand, squeeze glutes at top.
mistakes: Bending knees too much turns it into a conventional deadlift.
Rounding the back instead of hinging at hips.
Not going deep enough — the stretch is the stimulus.
romanian_deadlift.tip: Think 'push butt back to touch the wall behind you' — that cues the hip hinge.

steps: Sit with back flat against pad, feet shoulder-width on platform.
Lower sled by bending knees until ~90° or slightly deeper.
Keep knees tracking toes, don't let them cave.
Press through mid-foot, stop just short of lockout.
Control the descent, don't crash the weight stack.
mistakes: Placing feet too high shifts work to glutes/hams, off quads.
Locking out knees at top removes tension and risks joint stress.
Lower back rounding off the pad under heavy load.
leg_press.tip: Foot placement matters: lower = more quads, higher = more glutes/hams.

steps: Sit, back against pad, ankles on roller, knee at machine pivot.
Curl heels toward glutes, driving through heels.
Squeeze hamstrings at full contraction.
Return slowly, resisting the weight on the way up.
Keep hips pinned to the seat throughout.
mistakes: Hips lifting off the pad reduces hamstring isolation.
Dorsiflexing ankles (toes up) shifts work to calves.
Fast, uncontrolled negatives waste the eccentric.
seated_leg_curl.tip: Point toes slightly (plantarflex) to bias hamstrings over calves.

steps: Stand on platform edge, heels hanging off, balls of feet on.
Lower heels until you feel a deep stretch in calves.
Press up onto tiptoes as high as possible.
Hold the top contraction for 1-2 seconds.
Lower slowly, don't bounce out of the bottom.
mistakes: Bouncing reps uses Achilles tendon elasticity, not muscle.
Not going high enough — full plantarflexion is key.
Knees bending turns it into a soleus-only movement.
standing_calf_raise.tip: Straight knees = gastrocnemius focus. Add seated calf raises for soleus.

steps: Sit, feet on platform, knees slightly bent, grab handle.
Start with arms extended, shoulder blades protracted.
Pull handle to lower ribs, driving elbows back.
Retract shoulder blades hard at the end.
Return with control, allowing full stretch forward.
mistakes: Leaning back excessively turns it into a hip hinge.
Shrugging shoulders up instead of pulling back.
Not getting full protraction at the start.
seated_cable_row.tip: Pause 1 second at the peak contraction — mid-back responds well to time under tension.

steps: Stand or sit, dumbbells at sides, palms facing forward.
Curl both dumbbells up, keeping elbows at sides.
Supinate (rotate pinkies up) as you curl for peak contraction.
Squeeze at top, lower with control.
Full extension at bottom for stretch.
mistakes: Swinging dumbbells with shoulders/hips.
Elbows drifting forward reduces tension.
Not supinating misses the biceps' rotational function.
dumbbell_curl.tip: Supinate hard at the top — the biceps both flexes the elbow AND supinates the forearm.

steps: Lie face down, ankles under roller, knees just off pad.
Curl heels to glutes, hips pressed into pad.
Squeeze hamstrings at top.
Lower slowly, don't kick the weight down.
Keep toes pointed (plantarflexed) throughout.
mistakes: Hips lifting off the pad = glutes taking over.
Dorsiflexed ankles (toes up) shifts to calves.
Fast eccentric wastes hamstring growth stimulus.
leg_curl.tip: If your gym only has lying curl, it's fine — just keep hips glued down.

steps: Stand on raised surface, heels hanging, hold for balance.
Lower heels deep for full stretch.
Press up onto tiptoes, hold peak contraction.
Lower slowly, 2-3 seconds down.
Keep knees straight (or slightly bent for soleus bias).
mistakes: Bouncing reps — the Achilles does the work, not the muscle.
Partial range — you need full stretch AND full contraction.
Bending knees too much on a standing raise shifts to soleus.
calf_raise.tip: Do straight-leg for gastroc, bent-knee (seated) for soleus. Both matter for full calves.
